subject: biology
title: Diabetes
key_idea: In type 1 diabetes the pancreas does not make enough insulin, so it is treated with insulin injections. In type 2 diabetes the body cells no longer respond to insulin, so diet and exercise help. Obesity is a risk factor for type 2.

blocks.text: Diabetes is a disorder in which blood glucose concentration cannot be controlled. There are two types, with different causes.

items: The pancreas fails to produce enough insulin.
Glucose cannot move into the cells properly, so blood glucose concentration becomes very high.
It is normally treated with insulin injections.
The insulin causes cells to take in glucose and liver and muscle to store it as glycogen, so blood glucose falls.
Type 1: the pancreas does not make enough insulin.
Treatment: insulin injections.

blocks.text: In type 2 diabetes the problem is not making insulin. It is the response of the cells.

items.meaning: The body cells no longer respond properly to the insulin the pancreas produces.

items: The pancreas still makes insulin, often more than normal, but the cells (including liver and muscle cells) absorb less glucose.
Blood glucose concentration stays high, which stimulates the pancreas to release even more insulin.
Common treatments are a carbohydrate-controlled diet, an exercise regime and losing body mass.
Medicines such as metformin can also lower blood glucose.

rows: The pancreas does not make enough insulin
Body cells no longer respond to insulin
Diet, exercise and losing mass, sometimes medicine

items: On a graph, blood glucose in a person without diabetes rises after a meal, then returns to normal.
In a person with diabetes it rises higher and stays high for longer.
Type 2: the cells do not respond to insulin, so glucose stays in the blood.
Treatment: carbohydrate-controlled diet, exercise and losing mass.

blocks.text: Obesity is a risk factor for type 2 diabetes. Body mass index (BMI) compares a person's mass with their height.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating body mass index from mass and height.
diagram.question: A person has a body mass of **{m} kg** and a height of **{h} m**. Calculate their BMI. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

items: A higher body mass or BMI is linked to a greater chance of developing type 2 diabetes.
Other factors also affect the chance, such as age, diet, exercise and genes.
Losing body mass and exercising help to control type 2 diabetes.
Recommendations about lifestyle can involve social and ethical issues, such as cost to the health service and people's freedom to choose.
BMI = mass ÷ height². Square the height first.
Obesity is linked to type 2 diabetes, but it is not the only factor.

sections.heading: High blood glucose and body cells

blocks.text: In untreated diabetes the blood glucose concentration is very high. This affects the water balance of the body cells.

items: The blood is more concentrated, with a lower water potential, than the solution inside the cells.
Water moves out of the cells by osmosis, through the partially permeable cell membrane.
The cells become dehydrated and shrivel.
High blood glucose makes the blood more concentrated than the cells.
Water leaves the cells by osmosis.

checks.q: Explain why a person with type 2 diabetes often has a higher blood insulin concentration than a person without diabetes.
checks.a: Their cells absorb less glucose, so blood glucose stays high. This causes the pancreas to release more insulin.

checks.q: Describe two lifestyle changes that help to control type 2 diabetes.
checks.a: Any two from: eat less carbohydrate or sugar; lose body mass; take more exercise.

checks.q: A person has a body mass of 90 kg and a height of 1.8 m. Calculate their BMI to 1 decimal place.

worked_example.question:
The body cells of a person with Type 2 diabetes do not respond to insulin. A person with Type 2 diabetes often has a higher blood insulin concentration than a non-diabetic person.

Explain why.
answer_points: Cells / liver / muscles absorb less glucose (or convert less glucose to glycogen). Do not accept "no absorption".
So glucose concentration in the blood remains high (does not decrease).
The high blood glucose stimulates the pancreas to release more insulin.
worked_example.tip: Three linked steps: cells absorb less glucose, blood glucose stays high, the pancreas releases more insulin.

worked_example.question:
A hospital patient was tested for diabetes.

A nurse recorded his mass and height. His mass was 124 kg and his height was 1.8 m.

Calculate the BMI of this patient.
answer_points: Evaluation: BMI = 38.27 (accept 38 or 38.3; any correct rounding).
Correct answer with no working gains 2 marks. 68.9 (height not squared) gains 1 mark.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the substitution with the height squared and one for the evaluation.

blocks.text: Edexcel also uses the waist-to-hip ratio to assess the risk of type 2 diabetes.

blocks.label: Waist-to-hip ratio
blocks.formula: waist-to-hip ratio = waist circumference ÷ hip circumference
where: waist circumference and hip circumference are measured in the same unit, for example cm

items.text: A waist of 90 cm and hips of 100 cm.

blocks.text: Besides BMI and waist-to-hip ratio, age, diet, exercise regime, ethnicity and genetic makeup also affect the probability of developing type 2 diabetes.

worked_example.question:
Diabetes can be Type 1 or Type 2.

Describe two differences between the treatments for Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes.
answer_points: Type 1 diabetes is treated with insulin.
Type 2 diabetes is controlled through diet and exercise (allow: medication to lower blood glucose; reduce sugar intake; lose weight).
worked_example.tip: One mark for each type. Write about treatment only.

worked_example.question:
A gene mutation may be involved in the development of type 1 diabetes.

Outline the treatment of type 1 diabetes.
answer_points: Insulin is given by injections or by a pump.
Blood (or urine) glucose concentration is monitored.
Carbohydrate intake in the diet is controlled.
Exercise after eating helps to lower blood glucose.
worked_example.tip: Any three points score one mark each. Name the insulin treatment and one way of managing diet or monitoring.

blocks.text: (Supplement) Insulin is only part of the treatment of type 1 diabetes.

items: Insulin is given by **injections** or by a **pump** that delivers it through the day.
Blood glucose concentration is **monitored**.
Carbohydrate intake is counted and matched to activity.
Exercise after eating helps to lower blood glucose.
A pancreas transplant or an artificial pancreas can also be used.
